title: Intermittent test failures are bugs until proven otherwise: investigate each
description:
First widened run of epic-9pd, 2026-09-17. bzx's integrated gate ran while three workers (oe0, pbb, q1e) were still thinking in their own worktrees. Every package took two to four times its usual wall clock - internal/reconcile 848s against 388s on a quiet machine, internal/runstate 601s against 164s - and one timing-sensitive test failed: TestALaunchPastTheCallBoundProducesNoVerdictAndNoTeardown in internal/exec/herdr.

bzx's own change touched internal/cli and nothing else. It was refused for a test in a package it never went near, because the run's own concurrency had saturated the machine. That is a verdict about the machine wearing a verdict's clothes.

Two fixes, one done: the specific test sampled a race it had set up itself (herdr completes the launch at 800ms, the client gives up at 300ms) and won it only while the machine was idle; it now waits for the spawn with a deadline. The systemic half is open. The gate declares -parallel 12, which assumes an idle host; at width N it is competing with N-1 agents and whatever they compile and test. Candidate shapes: derive the gate's parallelism from the width, quiesce dispatch while a gate runs, or give the gate a machine of its own (which is what Phase 4's cloud host would do for free).

Also worth a sweep: this is unlikely to be the only load-sensitive test, and each one is a tick refused at random until it is found.
notes:
2026-09-17 23:58 - The gate's resource envelope is a MEMORY problem as well as a CPU one, and it is now hitting the orchestrator itself.

During epic-9pd's gates the system went low on memory twice, and each time the harness killed the operator's watcher as collateral - the run was never in trouble, but the thing watching it died. 'go test -parallel 12' spawns twelve test binaries at once; on this host that is enough to trigger the memory guard.

Two consequences worth designing for, not just the slowness already recorded here:
- A gate can kill things that are not the gate. Anything sharing the host - the watcher, another agent, the operator's editor - is a candidate victim.
- The failure is silent from the run's point of view. The run kept going and never knew its observer was gone, which is the stall shape this project keeps rediscovering: the orchestration was fine, the monitoring died.

Mitigation taken now: the watcher was rewritten leaner (no python per poll, 120s beat) and relaunched. That treats the symptom. The fix belongs here - the gate's parallelism should account for the host it shares, whether that means deriving it from the width, quiescing while gating, or Phase 4's separate machine.
2026-09-18 06:53 - Fourth load-sensitive test found, same pattern, same cost.

TestAReleaseNeverRecordsTheOperatorIdentity (internal/reconcile/settle_identity_test.go) kills a supervisor then immediately asks a fresh reconciler to release the attempt. Settle refuses a live attempt by design, so the test depends on the kill landing before the next probe - true on an idle machine, false under gate load. It refused tick sqx, whose change touched close-out CI gating and nothing near attempt liveness. Fixed by waiting for the precondition rather than sampling it.

The four so far: TestALaunchPastTheCallBoundProducesNoVerdictAndNoTeardown (herdr, refused bzx), TestTheStallWarningChangesNoVerdict (reconcile, refused 7zs), TestFactoryDeployAndSetupAreWired (cli, hung 45m on a wedged docker daemon and refused oe0), and this one. Every one of them refused a tick whose own change was somewhere else entirely.

That is the cost this tick is really about: not that gates are slow, but that a slow gate REFUSES INNOCENT WORK, and each refusal costs an hour-long re-gate to discover it was nothing. A sweep for the remaining ones is worth more than it sounds.
2026-09-18 07:56 - Fifth: TestAPendingCIThatNeverConcludesIsBounded (sqx's own test). Its 200ms GateTimeout bounded the fixture's gate COMMAND as well as the CI wait; the command exceeded 200ms under load and the test reported a gate error for tick a2 instead of the CI refusal it asserts. Worked around at f436737; the underlying conflation of two bounds is filed as 8kz.

Five for five, every one refusing a tick whose change was elsewhere: bzx, 7zs, oe0, sqx (twice). The run has now spent more wall time re-gating innocent work than the work itself took.
2026-09-18 08:58 - Parallelisation tick x73 (epic t8u) is blocked on this one. Raising concurrency makes machine contention worse, and five tests in this suite already return verdicts about the machine rather than the tree - parallelising before they are fixed would manufacture more false refusals at an hour of re-gating each.

Two of the load sources are the suite's own: concurrent_fetch_test.go runs two unthrottled 'for { git fetch }' goroutines that each burn a core for the length of the test. Tick 1qy replaces them with a deterministic seam, which is a fix for this tick as much as a speed-up.
2026-09-19 13:45 - 2026-09-19 — SIXTH occurrence, and it refused 9fc in epic ncv.

    --- FAIL: TestTheWaitUsesTheExecutorsCadenceNotTheRuns (79.42s)
        feed_test.go:286: the wait never slept; the executor's cadence never applied

9fc's change is TypeScript plus one closeout test. It has nothing to do with poll cadence. Same shape as the five before it: a slow gate REFUSES INNOCENT WORK.

What I could establish, so the next person does not redo it:

- It fails ONLY inside the full package at -parallel 12, where ~80 tests each fork git and worker processes. internal/reconcile took 845s in the failing gate against 410s for a clean run of the same tree.
- It passes 3/3 in isolation and 6/6 under synthetic CPU load at load average 13-29. So the trigger is PROCESS and fd contention, not CPU starvation.
- The test is not naively racy: holdingInspector forces 2 holds, so Inspect should return 'running' twice and the wait should sleep twice deterministically. len(slept)==0 means the wait never polled a held job AT ALL, which is a stronger failure than a missed deadline and is the thing to investigate. Suspects, in order: the attempt settling before the first poll despite the hold, the wrap not being applied to the attempt that ran, or RunProtected returning before dispatch under contention.
- It is NOT a regression from dh1's liveness probe: the same test passes on the same tree in isolation, repeatedly.

The gate's evidence is keyed by the commit it ran on, so an unchanged tree keeps the failure — a false refusal of this kind cannot be cleared by re-running. That is a second cost of these tests beyond the lost hour, and it is worth stating on this tick: EVERY false refusal forces a tree change to clear.
2026-09-19 14:17 - 2026-09-19 — SEVENTH occurrence, reported independently by 9fc's own worker (finding f2bac39d):

    TestAStoppedAttemptSPreservedWorkReachesTheNextAttempt
    'the run's feed never said a1's wall clock fired'
    reconcile package: 38 wall minutes against ~5 CPU minutes

Then passed in isolation (20s) and in a full -parallel 12 re-run (300s). Same signature as the sixth (TestTheWaitUsesTheExecutorsCadenceNotTheRuns): fails only under package-level contention, passes alone.

The worker's own observation is the useful part: the Makefile header ALREADY names host load plus 'the one wall-clock-sensitive test' as the known exposure. It is documented and it still fired and still refused innocent work. Documenting a known flake is not a mitigation.

Caveat on both of today's occurrences, recorded so the evidence is not overstated: the orchestrator had four runaway CPU busy-loops on the host for part of this window, left behind by a failed cleanup in a load experiment. Some of the contention was self-inflicted. That does not explain the earlier five, and it does not make these tests robust, but a future reading of 'it fails at 845s' should know the host was being abused at the time.
2026-09-19 17:48 - 2026-09-19 — EIGHTH occurrence, and this one blocked Phase 4's close-out.

    prior_snapshots_test.go:58: the refusal is 'attempt 1 of a1 cannot be
    addressed and has not settled: nobody can say whether it is running, which
    is not the same as nothing running', want collect_failed

CI, go job, on the epic PR head carrying the close-out's own commits. internal/reconcile took 190s there. Passes 3/3 locally on the same tree.

The failure text is worth keeping because it names the mechanism exactly: the attempt had not SETTLED when the test asked. The test wants the settled refusal (collect_failed) and gets the honest 'I cannot tell yet'. That is the cy2 shape stated by the code itself — the test samples a state that is still resolving.

Running total of the class: 8. Today alone contributed 4 (TestTheWaitUsesTheExecutorsCadenceNotTheRuns, TestAStoppedAttemptSPreservedWorkReachesTheNextAttempt, three timing failures in run-workflow.test.ts, and this). Every one refused work whose own change was elsewhere, and this one held an epic's hand-over.

Note the cost shape has now been observed end to end: a false refusal cannot be cleared by re-running (evidence is keyed by the commit), so it forces either a tree change or a CI re-run, and in this case it stopped a close-out that had already passed its own integrated gate.
2026-09-19 19:20 - 2026-09-19 — occurrences NINE and TEN, both in 3q0's integrated gate on epic ncv, load average ~22, on code byte-identical to a commit CI had passed 4/4 an hour earlier.

9: TestALostAttemptIsReleasedByAPersonAndTheNextRunDispatchesANewOne
   repair_test.go:234: 'attempt 1 of a1 is running — the executor can still address it'
   The fake worker had not died yet when the test released it. Passes 2/2 alone.

10: TestCancelIsIdempotent — and this one was NOT a slow test. It was a REAL BUG that only load exposed: Cancel stamped the acceptance time twice on the first call (record, then ack), so the ack could claim a later second than the record it acknowledged. Fixed and given a deterministic test (TestACancelAcknowledgesTheTimeItRecorded, an advancing clock) that fails every time on the old code.

That second one is the lesson worth keeping on this tick: not every load-sensitive failure is a timing-sensitive TEST. Some are timing-sensitive CODE that a quiet machine hides. Treating the whole class as 'flaky, re-run it' would have buried a genuine defect. The check that separated them was cheap — does the failure violate an ordering that cannot happen (a later call returning an earlier time)? — and it is worth doing before any re-run.
2026-09-19 19:50 - 2026-09-19 — CORRECTION to occurrences 7 and 8, and an eleventh.

TestAStoppedAttemptSPreservedWorkReachesTheNextAttempt (prior_snapshots_test.go:58) was recorded here twice as a load-sensitive TEST. It was not. It failed a third time on CI and was traced to a real race in the local executor's observe: settlement was read BEFORE liveness, so a supervisor that settled and exited in between was reported LOST — and lost makes a run refuse and stop. Fixed on epic/ncv (ca77e44) with a deterministic test that reproduces the CI message word for word against the old order.

That makes two of today's 'flaky tests' real defects (this and TestCancelIsIdempotent), both of the same kind: a value read at one moment and trusted at a later one. Out of eleven occurrences filed here, two were code. That ratio is the argument for checking each one rather than re-running — and specifically for asking whether the failure shows something impossible (a later call returning an earlier time; a finished process reported as unknown).
2026-09-19 19:57 - 2026-09-19 — OPERATOR POLICY: 'generally assume flaky = bug'.

This tick was a bucket for 'load-sensitive tests'. That framing was wrong often enough to matter: 2 of the 11 occurrences filed here were races in PRODUCTION code (herdr Cancel's double stamp; subprocess observe reading settlement before liveness), and the second one stops real runs. Both were visible only on the 2-vCPU CI runner.

So the rule now: an intermittent failure is a defect in the code until an investigation shows otherwise. Re-running is for gathering evidence, never the fix; widening a timeout is never the fix.

STILL UNEXPLAINED, and each owed a real investigation rather than a re-run:
  - TestTheWaitUsesTheExecutorsCadenceNotTheRuns — empty 'slept': the wait never polled a held job at all, despite holdingInspector forcing two holds. That is an impossible outcome, which is the signature of a real bug.
  - TestALostAttemptIsReleasedByAPersonAndTheNextRunDispatchesANewOne — 'attempt is running, the executor can still address it'.
  - run-workflow.test.ts: 'expected undefined to be run_wf_121' and 'length 1 but got 2' (an extra run_event).
  - TestNoCIOnThePRRefusesUnsatisfiable (Go, CI only).

Resolved as genuine test defects, for contrast: lan (read the engine's status once instead of waiting — fixed to wait on the observable).
2026-09-20 01:44 - 2026-09-19 23:43 — THREE more, in one gate, and the host explains all of them.

epic dha's gate for 6na ran 23:05:50 -> 23:42:46 (37 minutes for a job that costs 3m26s idle) and failed:
  TestCollectCarriesAnUnparseableBlockAsAProblemNotSilence — 'timed out after 30s waiting for the attempt to settle' (the test itself took 113s)
  TestDeployWaitsForTheContainerRolloutToServeTheNewImage — rollout not confirmed (62s)
  TestTheSettlementWaitIsBoundedByTheAttemptsOwnWallClock — 'the wait for an attempt that never settles did not end: it is not bounded' (72s)

Package wall times against their usual: exec/subprocess 1254s (~200s), factory 1202s (~170s), runstate 1389s (~100s). Six to thirteen times slower.

Load average 171, five-minute 262 — mostly ANOTHER repository's epic run on the same machine (32 node/vitest processes and a bun suite under ~/.herdr/worktrees/canonify), plus this run's own workers.

Under the operator's rule these are still bugs, and the shape is the same in all three: a test that waits a FIXED 30s for something whose cost is a function of host speed. The repair is to wait on the observable (the attempt settling, the rollout serving) with a bound derived from the run's own clock, not a constant. But the trigger tonight was not the tests being marginal — it was a host running at a tenth of its speed, which is w1j.

Note for whoever fixes these: 'the wait is not bounded' failing is not evidence the bound is broken. It is evidence the bound was longer than the test's patience, which is the same confusion between 'slow' and 'wedged' that dh1 and ad4 were about.
2026-09-20 11:11 - 2026-09-20 09:11 — FOUR more in one gate (80x, epic dha), gate ran 08:38:05 -> 09:10:41 (32 min) at load 36 with 23 foreign node processes and two of our own test runs on the host:

  TestALaunchPastTheCallBoundProducesNoVerdictAndNoTeardown — 'left no record: open /var/folders/...' (7.33s)
  TestAStoppedAttemptSPreservedWorkReachesTheNextAttempt — 'still reads running 6s past the wall clock of 10s' (59.09s)
  TestAnAbandonedAttemptIsMeasuredBeforeTheRunWalksAway — 'a2 was never announced as abandoned, so this run is not the shape the test is about' (42.19s)
  TestAWedgedAttemptIsDistinguishableFromAWorkingOne — 374.64s

Package wall times: internal/exec/herdr 628s. The reconcile package's own liveness test taking 374s is the clearest single number here: it is seconds of work.

Two of these are already spoken for and should NOT be counted as new evidence for this tick:
  - TestAStoppedAttemptSPreservedWorkReachesTheNextAttempt is what 8jl fixes (the grace must count from the bound firing, not from dispatch). 8jl merged to main as a1deef8c but is NOT yet folded into epic/dha, so this tree still has the old behaviour. Expect it to stop failing after the next fold.
  - TestAnAbandonedAttemptIsMeasuredBeforeTheRunWalksAway and TestAWedgedAttemptIsDistinguishableFromAWorkingOne are dh1's liveness tests, and 9pz changed when a worker is released. If they keep failing on a QUIET host after the fold, they are a real 9pz/dh1 interaction and not this tick — investigate them there rather than adding them here.

That is the discipline this tick needs as it grows: a load-shaped failure is only evidence for cy2 if it survives a quiet host. The next restart runs on a quieter machine with 8jl and 3mp folded in, which is the experiment.
acceptance_criteria: A gate's verdict does not change with the number of workers running beside it: the same tree gates the same way at width 1 and width 4. Either the gate's resource envelope accounts for the run's width, or the run does not gate while it holds live attempts. The repository's timing-sensitive tests are identified and made to wait for conditions rather than sample them.
